_link.title: I can explain the role of the split ring commutator in a DC motor

toLevel2.stem: What is the main purpose of the split ring commutator in a DC motor?
toLevel2.answer: To reverse the current direction in the coil every half turn
distractors: To increase the voltage supplied to the coil
To reduce friction between the coil and magnets
To connect the motor to an alternating current supply

toLevel2.stem: How often does the split ring commutator reverse the current through the coil?
toLevel2.answer: Every half turn of the coil
distractors: Every full turn of the coil
Every quarter turn of coil
Only when motor first starts

toLevel2.stem: What would happen to the coil of a DC motor if the split ring commutator were removed?
toLevel2.answer: The coil would stop after rotating partway
distractors: The coil would spin faster than normal
The coil would produce an electric current
The coil would rotate in the other direction

toLevel2.stem: Which components make and break electrical contact with the split ring commutator?
distractors: Permanent magnets
Copper wire leads
Insulating spacers

toLevel2.stem: The split ring commutator is a conducting ring that is split into how many separate halves?
toLevel2.answer: Two halves separated by insulating gaps
distractors: Four quarters separated by metal strips
Three thirds separated by rubber gaskets
Six segments separated by plastic dividers

toLevel2.stem: The split ring commutator reverses the {{blank:1}} through the coil every half turn so the coil rotates {{blank:2}}.
Without a commutator, the coil of a DC motor would rotate to the {{blank:1}} position and then {{blank:2}}.
The brushes press against the {{blank:1}} to maintain an electrical connection as the {{blank:2}} rotates.
The split ring commutator ensures the force on each side of the coil always acts in the same rotational direction.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: The split ring commutator increases the strength of the magnetic field inside the motor.
distractors: True

toLevel3.stem: Why must the current through the coil be reversed every half turn for the motor to spin continuously?
toLevel3.answer: So the forces on the coil sides always push in the same rotational direction
distractors: So the magnetic field strength inside the motor is kept constant
So the coil does not overheat from carrying too much current
So the brushes do not lose contact with the commutator ring

toLevel3.stem: At what position of the coil does the commutator switch which brush contacts which half of the split ring?
toLevel3.answer: When the coil passes through the vertical position
distractors: When the coil is in the horizontal position
When the coil reaches maximum angular velocity
When the coil completes one full rotation cycle

toLevel3.stem: What is the relationship between the commutator switching and the torque on the coil?
toLevel3.answer: The commutator switches when the torque on the coil is zero
distractors: The commutator switches when torque is at its maximum
The commutator switches when the coil is accelerating
The commutator switches when the current is at maximum

toLevel3.stem: If the split ring commutator were replaced with a complete, unbroken ring, what would the motor do?
toLevel3.answer: Oscillate back and forth instead of rotating continuously
distractors: Rotate continuously but in the opposite direction only
Rotate at exactly double the speed of normal operation
Produce a stronger force on each side of the spinning coil

toLevel3.stem: Why are the gaps in the split ring commutator aligned with the brushes when the coil is vertical?
toLevel3.answer: So the current reversal occurs when the coil plane is parallel to the field
distractors: So the coil receives maximum current at the vertical position
So the magnetic flux through the coil is at its minimum value
So the brushes experience the least amount of frictional wear

toLevel3.stem: How does the commutator ensure forces on the coil always produce rotation in one direction?
toLevel3.answer: It reverses the current so each side always experiences a force in the same rotational sense
distractors: It increases the current each half turn to overcome the opposing torque on the coil
It switches the magnetic poles of the permanent magnets around the coil each cycle
It disconnects the coil from the supply whenever the torque would act in the wrong way

toLevel3.stem: When the coil passes through the {{blank:1}} position, the torque is zero and the commutator {{blank:2}} the current direction.
Without the commutator, the coil would experience a torque that {{blank:1}} direction each half turn, causing it to {{blank:2}}.
The split ring commutator converts the {{blank:1}} supply into a current that alternates direction in the {{blank:2}}.
The commutator reverses the current at the instant when the plane of the coil is parallel to the magnetic field.
distractors: False

toLevel4.stem: A student builds a motor but accidentally installs the commutator so it switches the current when the coil is horizontal. What will happen?
toLevel4.answer: The coil will oscillate because the current reversal now opposes continuous rotation
distractors: The coil will rotate normally because current direction does not matter here
The coil will spin faster because the switching occurs at peak torque value
The coil will not move at all because the brushes cannot contact the ring

toLevel4.stem: In a DC motor, the coil has just passed through the vertical position and the commutator has switched contacts. What happens to the force on the side of the coil that was previously being pushed upward?
toLevel4.answer: Its current reverses so it is now pushed downward, maintaining the same rotation
distractors: Its current stays the same so it continues to be pushed in the upward direction
Its current reverses so it is pushed upward with twice the original force value
Its current drops to zero so no force acts on that side of the coil anymore

toLevel4.stem: A motor is running with the coil in the horizontal plane. At this instant, the torque is at its maximum. What role does the commutator play at this specific moment?
toLevel4.answer: No role; the commutator maintains the same current direction at this position
distractors: It reverses the current to maximise the torque on the coil at this point
It disconnects the coil from the supply to prevent overheating of the wire
It doubles the current to ensure the coil accelerates through this position

toLevel4.stem: A student replaces the DC supply of a motor with an AC supply while keeping the split ring commutator. What effect does this have on the motor's operation?
toLevel4.answer: The motor may not rotate smoothly because the AC reversal interferes with the commutator switching
distractors: The motor spins at exactly the same speed since the commutator fixes the issue
The motor produces twice the torque because both devices reverse the current flow
The motor works identically because AC and DC are interchangeable in all motors

toLevel4.stem: In a simple DC motor, the commutator switches the current at the vertical position where torque is zero. Why is this timing beneficial?
toLevel4.answer: The coil's inertia carries it through the zero-torque point before torque resumes
distractors: The coil experiences maximum acceleration at the exact point of zero torque
The magnetic field is strongest at the vertical position of the spinning coil
The brushes have the greatest friction at this position to slow the coil down

toLevel4.stem: Two identical motors are built, but Motor A has a split ring commutator while Motor B has a complete ring. If both are connected to the same DC supply, which statement is correct?
toLevel4.answer: Motor A rotates continuously; Motor B oscillates and stops
distractors: Both motors rotate continuously at the same speed value
Motor B rotates continuously; Motor A oscillates and stops
Neither motor rotates because DC cannot drive a motor

toLevel4.stem: A DC motor's commutator has worn down, causing intermittent contact with the brushes. Which observation would a student most likely make?
toLevel4.answer: The motor stutters and rotates unevenly due to interrupted current
distractors: The motor spins faster because less friction acts on the coil
The motor reverses direction each time contact is temporarily lost
The motor produces a stronger magnetic field around the coil wire

toLevel4.stem: At the vertical position the coil's {{blank:1}} carries it past the dead point, and the commutator ensures the {{blank:2}} is in the correct direction for continued rotation.
If the commutator switches at the wrong position, the torque will {{blank:1}} the rotation for part of each cycle, causing the motor to {{blank:2}}.
Replacing a split ring commutator with a complete ring means the current in the coil {{blank:1}} reverses, so the coil {{blank:2}} rotate continuously.

toLevel5.stem: A student argues that a split ring commutator is unnecessary if the DC supply is simply turned off and on at the right moments. Evaluate this claim.
toLevel5.answer: It is impractical because manual switching cannot match the precise timing the commutator achieves mechanically
distractors: It is correct because any method of reversing current will produce identical results
It is wrong because turning off the supply would reverse the magnetic field direction
It is correct because electronic switching is always less efficient than a commutator

toLevel5.stem: Modern brushless DC motors use electronic switching instead of a mechanical commutator. What advantage does this provide over a split ring commutator?
toLevel5.answer: Electronic switching eliminates brush wear and allows more precise timing of current reversal
distractors: Electronic switching removes the need to reverse current direction in the motor coils
Electronic switching makes the motor operate without any magnetic field being present
Electronic switching increases the strength of the permanent magnets inside the motor

toLevel5.stem: In a multi-coil DC motor, the commutator has many segments rather than just two halves. Why does this improve performance?
toLevel5.answer: More segments provide smoother torque because at least one coil always experiences near-maximum torque
distractors: More segments increase the voltage supplied to each individual coil in the motor
More segments eliminate the need for permanent magnets inside the motor housing
More segments allow the motor to operate using alternating current supply directly

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that a commutator is needed because the magnetic field reverses direction each half turn. Is this reasoning correct?
toLevel5.answer: No; the field stays constant but the coil sides swap position, requiring current reversal
distractors: Yes; the permanent magnets reverse their polarity as the coil rotates around
No; the commutator is needed because the coil changes speed each half rotation
Yes; the field lines change direction each time the coil crosses the vertical axis

toLevel5.stem: An engineer considers using slip rings instead of a split ring commutator in a DC motor. What would be the consequence?
toLevel5.answer: Slip rings maintain constant current direction, so the coil would oscillate instead of rotating
distractors: Slip rings would reverse the current more frequently, making the motor spin faster
Slip rings would produce the same continuous rotation as a split ring commutator
Slip rings would prevent any current from flowing through the coil of the motor

toLevel5.stem: Compare the operation of a commutator in a DC motor with its role in a DC generator. Which statement is correct?
toLevel5.answer: In a motor the commutator reverses DC to maintain rotation; in a generator it rectifies AC to output DC
distractors: The commutator performs exactly the same function in both motors and generators always
In a motor the commutator produces AC; in a generator it converts AC to mechanical energy
The commutator is only needed in motors; generators do not require any form of switching

toLevel5.stem: A student notices sparking at the brushes of a DC motor. Which explanation best accounts for this observation?
toLevel5.answer: The sudden breaking and making of contact at the commutator gaps causes brief arcs
distractors: The permanent magnets are too strong and are ionising the air near the brush
The coil is spinning too slowly for the brushes to maintain smooth sliding contact
The carbon brushes are generating static electricity through friction with the ring

toLevel5.stem: Analyse why the commutator must be rigidly fixed to the coil rather than rotating independently.
toLevel5.answer: The switching must be synchronised with the coil's orientation to reverse current at the correct position
distractors: A freely rotating commutator would spin too fast for the brushes to maintain any contact
The commutator must be fixed so it does not contribute extra mass to the rotor assembly
A freely rotating commutator would generate its own magnetic field opposing the main one
